findings.highlight: I hope I’ll be able to penetrate the fortress
findings.evidenceJa: セイバーの牙城をうち破れればいいのだが
findings.governingReading: He hopes the calm mood will let him break through Saber’s defenses.
findings.explanation: Penetrate the fortress is stilted and gives the playful stronghold metaphor an unintended sexual cast.

findings.highlight: what should we do if we win the Holy Grail War
findings.evidenceJa: 聖杯を手に入れたらどうするか
findings.governingReading: What should they do once they obtain the Grail?
findings.explanation: The English repeats winning the war and removes the question about what to do with the prize afterward.

findings.highlight: I don’t care who uses the Holy Grail.
findings.evidenceJa: 聖杯の使い道なんてどうでもいいわ
findings.governingReading: Illya does not care what use is made of the Grail.
findings.explanation: The English changes indifference to the Grail’s use into indifference about the identity of its user.

findings.highlight: Saber’s acting in a complicated manner
findings.evidenceJa: その様子がただ事ではない
findings.governingReading: Her state is clearly no ordinary matter.
findings.explanation: The awkward English weakens the visible gravity that makes Rin and Illya stop arguing.

findings.highlight: I do not know how powerful the Holy Grail is.
findings.evidenceJa: 聖杯がどれほどの許容範囲を持っているかは知らない
findings.governingReading: She does not know the range or scope of what the Grail can accommodate.
findings.explanation: The English replaces uncertainty about the Grail’s applicable scope with a generic power-level question.

findings.highlight: Such whining fills my head.
findings.evidenceJa: そんな弱音が、脳裏を占めた
findings.governingReading: That fainthearted hope takes over his thoughts.
findings.explanation: Whining miscasts Shirou’s self-aware wish that Saber remain silent as a sound or complaint rather than his own weak thought.

findings.highlight: the girl who took that oath pulling out the sword
findings.evidenceJa: あの聖剣を手にした彼女
findings.governingReading: the woman who took up that holy sword, read as “oath”
findings.explanation: The English invents an act of pulling out a sword and fails to preserve the single holy-sword/oath expression.

findings.highlight: tilts her head not believing her own words
findings.evidenceJa: 自分の言葉に首を傾げた
findings.governingReading: She tilts her head at her own words.
findings.explanation: The English asserts disbelief where the active Japanese only stages Rin pausing over the contradiction she has voiced.

findings.highlight: you’re respected as a heroic spirit
findings.evidenceJa: 英霊として奉られている
findings.governingReading: one is enshrined or worshipped as a Heroic Spirit
findings.explanation: Respected weakens the supernatural posthumous status Rin uses to explain why a Heroic Spirit cannot ordinarily intervene by choice.

findings.highlight: I have yet to become a complete Servant.
findings.evidenceJa: まだ、完全にサーヴァントになった訳ではない
findings.governingReading: She has not yet fully become a Servant.
findings.explanation: The English makes Saber an incomplete instance of the class instead of preserving the unfinished temporal transition central to her contract.

findings.highlight: a ritual to give their existence to the world after they die
findings.evidenceJa: 死後の自分を明け渡す儀式
findings.governingReading: a rite that surrenders one’s posthumous self to the World
findings.explanation: Existence broadens the object of surrender and weakens the contract’s specific claim on the person after death.

findings.highlight: they become Servants to pay for these riches.
findings.evidenceJa: 死後は英霊として貰った財を返す
findings.governingReading: after death they repay what they received as Heroic Spirits, read here as “Servants”
findings.explanation: The English keeps only the ruby term and removes the passage’s deliberate Heroic Spirit/Servant layering.

findings.highlight: We summon Servants by stealing the debt liability from the world.
findings.evidenceJa: 返済金額を横からマスターに掠め取られて使役されてる
findings.governingReading: Masters intercept the repayment owed and use the Heroic Spirit as a servant.
findings.explanation: The English assigns the theft to “we,” invents the World as its source, and omits that the appropriated repayment is the Servant’s enforced labor.

findings.highlight: they’re summoned as heroic spirits
findings.evidenceJa: 英霊として使役される
findings.governingReading: they are made to serve as Heroic Spirits, read as “familiars”
findings.explanation: The English removes both compulsory service and the familiar reading that motivates Shirou’s summary.

findings.highlight: she became a heroic spirit after she died
findings.evidenceJa: 死後も英霊として守護者なんてモノを続けている
findings.governingReading: after death she continues serving as a guardian in the form of a Heroic Spirit
findings.explanation: The English omits the ongoing guardian service that Shirou imagines as the cost of Saber’s supposed bargain.

findings.highlight: I would become a heroic spirit after I died
findings.evidenceJa: 死後は守護者になってもよい
findings.governingReading: she accepted becoming a guardian after death
findings.explanation: The English collapses Saber’s promised role as a guardian into the broader Heroic Spirit category.

findings.highlight: pay for it with life after death
findings.evidenceJa: 死後の自分を売り渡します
findings.governingReading: they sell their posthumous selves in payment
findings.explanation: The malformed English suggests paying with life after death and obscures the surrender of the self to future service.

findings.highlight: I would wield my sword as a heroic spirit after my death
findings.evidenceJa: あらゆるモノの為に剣を執ろう
findings.governingReading: she would take up her sword for all things as a Heroic Spirit after death
findings.explanation: The English removes the universal beneficiary of the service Saber offers in exchange for the Grail.

findings.highlight: A lone king whose reign ended in betrayal.
findings.evidenceJa: 裏切りで終わった王
findings.governingReading: A king whose end came in betrayal, with no one to attend her.
findings.explanation: The English shifts betrayal from the king’s personal end to the end of her reign and weakens the deathbed image.

findings.highlight: if she wishes to prolong her life
findings.evidenceJa: ここでは死ねない。こんな終わりを望んだ訳じゃない
findings.governingReading: “I cannot die here. This is not the ending I wanted,” Shirou imagines.
findings.explanation: The English turns Shirou’s projected direct thought into a conditional narrator statement and omits his imagined refusal of this ending.

findings.highlight: Time stopped for me, King Arthur, at the moment of death.
findings.evidenceJa: 死を迎える一瞬で止まっている筈です
findings.governingReading: Saber herself should be suspended at the instant she meets death.
findings.explanation: The English initially says time stopped, erasing the person/time distinction Shirou explicitly corrects on the next page.

findings.highlight: I have not yet reached that rank.
findings.evidenceJa: 私はまだその位置に達していません
findings.governingReading: She has not yet reached the state or position of the Heroic Spirit “main body.”
findings.explanation: Rank introduces a hierarchy of status instead of an unfinished ontological transition.

findings.highlight: return to that stopped point once I obtain the Holy Grail
findings.evidenceJa: 聖杯を求めた後、止まっている場所に戻っている
findings.governingReading: After seeking the Grail in another time, she returns to the point where she is suspended.
findings.explanation: The English says she returns after obtaining the Grail, contradicting the explanation that only successful acquisition ends the cycle and lets her die.

findings.highlight: summoned into various ages
findings.evidenceJa: あらゆる時間上に呼び出され
findings.governingReading: summoned in answer to calls across all points in time
findings.explanation: Various ages weakens the unrestricted temporal scope of Shirou’s tentative model.

findings.highlight: a clone made from their DNA
findings.evidenceJa: 細胞から作ったクローン
findings.governingReading: a clone made from a cell
findings.explanation: The English substitutes DNA for the concrete cell analogy.

findings.highlight: no matter how many times they are summoned into the same age
findings.evidenceJa: あらゆる時代に同時に呼び出されようと
findings.governingReading: even if summoned simultaneously into every era
findings.explanation: The English changes simultaneous manifestations across all eras into repeated summons within one era.

findings.highlight: Saber talks without much interest.
findings.evidenceJa: 淡々とセイバーは語る
findings.governingReading: Saber speaks matter-of-factly and without outward agitation.
findings.explanation: The English assigns lack of interest to Saber during the disclosure of her defining wish.

findings.highlight: my mind is spacing out
findings.evidenceJa: 愕然と意識が白くなって
findings.governingReading: His consciousness goes white with shock.
findings.explanation: Spacing out trivializes the acute bodily shock with casual language.

findings.highlight: she will continue to be summoned to fight
findings.evidenceJa: ただ戦うだけの現象となって使役され続ける
findings.governingReading: She will become a phenomenon that does nothing but fight and remain in service.
findings.explanation: The English removes Saber’s reduction from a person to a battle-only phenomenon and weakens continuous servitude to recurring summons.

findings.highlight: the ten years she fought can’t just disappear
findings.evidenceJa: 彼女の十年間を、嘘にする事だけはできない
findings.governingReading: They cannot turn the ten years she fought through into a lie.
findings.explanation: Disappear changes Shirou’s ethical objection to falsifying Saber’s lived struggle into a claim about temporal erasure.

findings.highlight: So why don’t you understand
findings.evidenceJa: なんだってそんな事に、おまえだけが気づいていない
findings.governingReading: Why are you the only one who cannot see that?
findings.explanation: The English omits Shirou’s crucial claim that everyone except Saber can recognize what she has already given.

findings.highlight: Don’t be ridiculous, you’ve already fulfilled more than your duty
findings.evidenceJa: そんなの、おまえはもう十分すぎるぐらいに果たしてる
findings.governingReading: You have already fulfilled that duty more than enough.
findings.explanation: mirror moon’s non-Realta conditional branch inserts a direct rebuke absent from the bound original Japanese line.

findings.highlight: You didn’t give up
findings.evidenceJa: 負けなかった
findings.governingReading: She was not defeated, even when betrayed and feared.
findings.explanation: The English changes Saber’s endurance as an undefeated king into an inward refusal to surrender.

findings.highlight: people will get happier the more they work for it
findings.evidenceJa: 人間ってのは頑張れば頑張るほど、幸せになれる
findings.governingReading: The more earnestly people strive, the more happiness they ought to be able to attain.
findings.explanation: Work for it makes happiness sound like a direct labor formula and weakens Shirou’s childish belief that effort should be rewarded.

findings.highlight: I’ll be able to try with all my powers
findings.evidenceJa: 俺は全力でこの戦いに
findings.governingReading: He will commit himself fully to this battle.
findings.explanation: The English omits the battle as the object and changes a declaration of commitment into the ability to try.

findings.highlight: The loud bell
findings.evidenceJa: 重い鈴の音
findings.governingReading: the heavy toll of a bell
findings.explanation: Loud replaces the warning sound’s weight and timbre.

findings.highlight: can be heard in the distance
findings.evidenceJa: さざ波のように響いてくる
findings.governingReading: The light scraping spreads and resounds like ripples.
findings.explanation: The English invents distance and removes the ripple-like multiplication that foreshadows encirclement.

findings.highlight: A strange sound.
findings.evidenceJa: ガシャガシャという音
findings.governingReading: a repeated hard metallic clatter
findings.explanation: The English replaces a concrete sound effect with an unspecified judgment.

findings.highlight: bugs crawling around a light trap
findings.evidenceJa: 誘蛾灯に群がる虫
findings.governingReading: insects swarming a moth-attracting lamp
findings.explanation: The English changes airborne swarming toward a light into crawling around a trap, weakening the approaching mob image.

findings.highlight: I can sense that many sources of magical energy surround this place.
findings.evidenceJa: 複数の人間によるモノだってのは感じ取れる
findings.governingReading: He can sense that the encircling magical energy comes from multiple humans.
findings.explanation: The English removes the apparently human origin whose conflict with their hollow lack of will drives the identification puzzle.

findings.highlight: Skimming quickly, I can at least count twenty.
findings.evidenceJa: ざっと感じ取れるだけでも二十
findings.governingReading: Even a rough magical sensing gives him about twenty.
findings.explanation: Skimming sounds like visual or textual inspection and obscures that twenty is an approximate sensed count.
